newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SOCIETE GENERALE MULLS LOCAL MARKET - C.BANK.
newsitem.headline: SOCIETE GENERALE MULLS LOCAL MARKET - C.BANK.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Thursday that France's Societe Generale was mulling a move into the local banking market but had not submitted any formal applications yet.
The country's Ministry of European Affiars reported on Wednesday that the French bank would be the first western bank to operate directly in Lithuania.

Central bank govenor Reinoldijus Sharkinas confirmed at a press conference that the bank was examining the Lithuanian market but said that it had no immediate plans to set up shop in the Baltic state.
"We have had several meetings with the representatives of the bank," Sharkinas said.
"So far they are investigating the market but I cannot say that they will come here immediately," he said.
He added that the bank might be considering a branch office but that it had submitted no official application.
Poland's Kredyt Bank last year became the first foreign bank to recieve permission to set up a branch office in Lithuania.
A number of Estonian banks have also expressed interest in moving south, either by acquiring stakes in Lithuanian banks or through the establishment of rep or branch offices.
Sharkinas said that the two big state-run banks slated for privatisation, the State Commercial bank and the Agriculture Bank, were being eyed by foreign investors.
But he said he did not think it would be a good idea if all of the country's banks were bought by foreign investors.
Foreign investors have majority stakes in the country's two largest private banks, Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank.
